questions.title: Which places are called the 'general area'?
questions.question: Pick all the places that are part of the 'general area' on a golf course.

choices.text: The green for a different hole

questions.explanation: The 'general area' is most of the golf course. It includes the fairway, the semi-rough, and greens and tee boxes for other holes. Bunkers and penalty areas are not in the general area.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Most of the golf course, except for bunkers, penalty areas, greens and teeing areas for the hole you are playing.
A sand pit on the golf course. It is not part of the general area.
Places like ponds or lakes. They are marked and not part of the general area.
The short grass you aim for when you hit your ball.
The longer grass next to the fairway.

questions.teachingTip: Show kids different parts of the course and help them name which are part of the general area.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids may think bunkers or penalty areas are in the general area.
Some may not realise the green for a different hole is the general area.

questions.title: What counts as the general area?
questions.question: Which of the following areas is included in the 'general area' according to the Rules of Golf? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Putting green for a different hole

questions.explanation: The general area is most of the course, including the fairway, semi-rough and rough, and any green or teeing area for a different hole. Bunkers and penalty areas are not part of the general area.
